lessons.title: Meet the three axes
body: A point in 3D needs three coordinates: X, Y, and Z. The axes helper colors them red, green, and blue. Positive X points right along the red axis; positive Y points up along green.

Object position is measured relative to its parent. Right now the mesh belongs directly to the scene, so its local coordinates are also its world coordinates. A unit can represent a meter, a centimeter, or another scale you choose consistently.
lessons.task: Move the cube 2 units along positive X.

quiz.question: How many numbers describe a 3D position?
quiz.explanation: A Vector3 stores x, y, and z.

lessons.title: Turn in radians
body: Three.js object rotations use radians. A full turn is 2π radians, a half turn is π, and a quarter turn is π/2. Math.PI gives JavaScript’s value of π.
Euler rotation has one angle for each axis. Rotate this cube around Z to tilt it in the image. For complex orientation changes, the order of rotations matters; we will meet quaternions later.
lessons.hint: Replace 0 with Math.PI / 4 on the last line.

quiz.question: How many radians make a full turn?

lessons.title: Stretch without rebuilding
body: An object starts with scale (1, 1, 1). Doubling one component stretches it along that local axis without rebuilding its geometry. A zero scale flattens that axis; negative scales also mirror it.
Geometry dimensions and object scale are separate. A box with height 1.6 and Y scale 2 has a displayed height of 3.2 units. Uniform scale uses the same multiplier on all axes.
lessons.task: Stretch the cube to twice its height with mesh.scale.y = 2.
lessons.hint: The scale property starts at 1, not 0.

quiz.question: What does scale (1, 1, 1) do?
options: Makes the object one pixel wide
quiz.explanation: Scale is a multiplier. Multiplying each dimension by 1 keeps its size.

lessons.title: Move a family of objects
body: A Group is a parent for related objects. Moving a parent moves its children, while each child keeps its position relative to that parent. These relative positions are local space; their final positions in the scene are world space.
The small sphere is 2 units to the right of its group. Move the group upward and both objects move together. This is how you build a vehicle with attached wheels or a planet with an orbiting moon.
lessons.task: Move the whole group up 1 unit.
lessons.hint: Edit group.position.y, not mesh.position.y or moon.position.y.

quiz.question: A child’s position is relative to…
quiz.explanation: A parent’s transform is combined with its child’s local transform.

lessons.title: Find the point between
body: Vectors can represent positions and directions. A direction becomes a unit vector when normalized: its length becomes 1 while its direction stays the same.

lerpVectors(a, b, t) chooses a position along the line from a to b. At t = 0 you get a; at t = 1 you get b; at t = 0.5 you get the midpoint. This is a useful building block for camera moves and transitions.
lessons.task: Set t to 0.5 to place the cube halfway between the two markers.

quiz.question: What does t = 1 return in lerpVectors(a, b, t)?
quiz.explanation: Interpolation starts at a when t is 0 and reaches b when t is 1.
